title: Sequence-level latency waterfall and regional fallback orchestration
creator: Nina Alvarez
description: Build token/sequence-level waterfall instrumentation, SLO derivations, and a Grafana dashboard to attribute latency across serving stages and visualize regional fallback and circuit-breaker state transitions. Deliver a playbook for runbook-driven load-shedding and automated fallback orchestration tied to the SLO engine.
background: We observed incidents where P99 sequence latency spiked during cross-region failover and admission changes. Existing dashboards show route-level p95/p99 but lack per-sequence stage attribution (prefix K/V cache hit, kernel execution, KV retrieval, network transfer) and a timeline view that correlates circuit state transitions with SLO breaches. This makes RCA slower and hamstrings automated fallback tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument per-sequence timing for: request-receive, prefix-kv-lookup, batching-queue-wait, kernel-exec, postprocess, response-emit
SLO derivation: compute sequence-p95 and p99 on token-normalized latency and on prefix-cache-hit vs miss subsets
Grafana dashboard with: sequence waterfall lane, stacked latency breakdown, region-fallback timeline, circuit-breaker state lane, and KV-hit filter toggle
Alert rule: sequence_p99 over 1.5x baseline for >5 minutes triggers automated canary fallback to adjacent region and opens incident channel
Playbook: documented steps for manual and automated rollback, traffic steering, and audit logging links
End-to-end e2e test that simulates partial region degradation and verifies telemetry emits, fallback triggers, and dashboard shows expected transitions
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define and standardize sequence timing spans (span names and tags) across runtime - lead: runtime team
Phase 2: Extend request tracer to capture per-token prefix/KV hit boolean and tokenized timing; emit to tracing backend and metrics aggregator
Phase 3: Add aggregation pipelines: compute per-sequence histograms and token-normalized percentiles in ClickHouse; add daily rollups
Phase 4: Build Grafana dashboard and alerting rules; wire to incident runbook
Phase 5: Synthetic chaos test (region throttle/blackhole) and measure fallback timing and success criteria
Phase 6: Gradual rollout to prod: start with 10% routes, monitor noise, then full rollout
telemetry_queries: ClickHouse: SELECT quantiles(0.5,0.95,0.99)(seq_latency_ms) AS q FROM sequences WHERE service='runner' AND region='$region' AND day>=today()-7 GROUP BY toStartOfHour(timestamp)

ClickHouse (split by component): SELECT component, quantile(0.99)(duration_ms) FROM sequence_spans WHERE component IN ('kv_lookup','kernel_exec','batch_wait','postprocess') AND trace_sample=1 GROUP BY component
Event correlation: join traces where circuit_state!='CLOSED' and seq_latency_ms>p99_baseline to produce event timeline for dashboard
dashboard_tiles: Sequence waterfall: stacked bars per sequence showing component contribution (kv_lookup, batch_wait, kernel_exec, postprocess)
Regional fallback timeline: compact lane per region showing fallback start/end, circuit open/close markers, and brief annotation of triggered rule
KV hit vs miss p95/p99: small multiples by route and region
Circuit-breaker state heatmap: percent time in OPEN/HALF_OPEN by shard and region
Admit rate and drop ratio correlated with sequence_p99: scatterplot to identify load-shedding side effects
Synthetic failover run: annotated replay track (for our chaos run)
rollout_plan: Start in staging with a 4-week synthetic campaign. Deploy instrumentation behind feature flag to prod with 1% traffic shadowing, then 10%, then 100% after 72h stable. Enable automated fallback in two phases: detection-only (alerts + runbook hint) then automated traffic reroute for low-latency tier. Coordinate with SRE on on-call rotation for first 2 weeks of automated fallback.
qa_notes: Unit test spans emitted with correct tags; integration tests verify aggregation pipeline computes expected percentiles when fed deterministic traces. Use local ClickHouse dataset generator to validate histogram boundaries. Run chaos tests in a private sandbox region before staging.
